title: Bacterial Growth
description: Calibrating OD₆₀₀ and comparing E. coli growth across sugars and mixtures

blocks.text:
Write a summary of this experiment, its objectives, and conclusions between one paragraph and one page in length.


In this experiment, we investigated the growth of the bacterium E.coli. By using a spectrophotometer, we can measure the optical density of E.coli in a solution of media. Over time, these measurements can be used to determine the growth rate of E.coli. We used a variety of different solutions of media, 0.2% sugar solutions of Glucose, Xylose, Sorbitol, Galactose, Rhamnose, Ribose and Arabinose. For each of the sugars, we also created mixtures of 4:1, 2:1 and 1:1 mixtures of the sugar and glucose. Our aim is to understand how bacteria responds to different environmental conditions to consume different sources of fuel that are available at the same time. 

We found that E.coli do not effectively metabolize all sugars within a day even though they may have very similar chemical structures. And the lag time (time to adapt to a new sugar) is quite consistent between sugars, where the ability to metabolize sorbitol was first, followed by arabinose and then xylose. We also observed that the growth of E.coli in a mixed solution of sugar and glucose would use use up the glucose first - following the growth curve of pure glucose, then lag and the secondary growth curve resembled the curve of the pure sugar.
Write a sensible protocol for the serial dilutions for the OD calibration.

between OD600 and absolute number of bacteria. You should also assess for what

cells/mL?

For line 5 which has a dilution of 10^-5, we counted 139 colonies 
and for line 6 which has a dilution of 10^-6 we counted 17 colonies.

The blank reading was at OD = 0.105
Line 5 corresponds to well A6 which had an OD of 0.103
Line 6 corresponds to well A7 which had an OD of 0.105

As these values are too low to accurately measure, we will scale up the number we counted. 17 and 139 show a fairly good order of magnitude difference we expected, so we can multiply 155 (an average between 170 and 139) by 10^4 to get to line 2 or well A2 which had an OD of 0.216. 

0.216 - 0.105 = 0.111, for 1550000 cells/ 10µL = 1.55*10^5 cells/ µL = 1.55*10^8 cells / mL

This is on the same order of magnitude with our rule of thumb that OD600 = 0.1 corresponds to 10^8 cells.

def invert_dict(input_dict):
    """Invert a dictionary ignore None values."""
    # Create an empty dictionary to store the inverted mapping
    output_dict = {}

    # Iterate over items in the input dictionary
    for key, value in input_dict.items():
        if value is not None:
            if value in output_dict:
                output_dict[value].append(key)
            else:
                output_dict[value] = [key]

    return output_dict

def multi_reg_plot(
    df41,
    conds,
    colors=colorcet.b_glasbey_category10,
    OD_range=None,
    show_regression=True,
    return_plot=True,
):
    """Perform regression for multiple conditions and, if asked,
    generate a plot with multiple conditions, with or without
    showing regression lines."""
    if return_plot:
        # Instantiate figure
        p = bokeh.plotting.figure(
            frame_width=400,
            frame_height=200,
            x_axis_label="time (hr)",
            y_axis_label="absorbance",
            y_axis_type="log",
            x_range=[0, 24],
            toolbar_location="above",
        )
    
        # Items we will place in the legend
        legend_items = []

        # Loop through conditions with pretty colors
        for cond, color in zip(conds, colors):
            # Instantiate plotted lines for a given condition
            lines = []
    
            # Loop through each well corresponding to the sugar
            for well in conditions[cond]:
                # A line of the time series of absorbance
                lines.append(
                    p.line(
                        x=df41["time (hr)"], y=df41[well] - df41["background"], line_color=color
                    )
                )
    
            # Add the lines to the legend
            legend_items.append((cond, lines))

    # Loop through and perform regressions
    fit_lines = []
    results = []
    for cond in conds:
        # Loop through each well corresponding to the sugar
        for trial, well in enumerate(conditions[cond]):
            # Get best fit curve for each OD range
            for diaux_phase, ODr in enumerate(OD_range[cond][trial]):
                try:
                    # Get best fit parameters
                    A0, r, t_range = fit_growth(df41, well, ODr)

                    # Time points for theoretical curve
                    t_theor = np.linspace(*t_range, 200)

                    # Theoretical absorbance
                    A_theor = exp_growth(t_theor, A0, r)

                    results.append(
                        dict(
                            condition=cond,
                            trial=trial,
                            diaux_phase=diaux_phase,
                            OD_low=ODr[0],
                            OD_high=ODr[1],
                            A0=A0,
                            r=r,
                        )
                    )

                    # Plot theoretical curve in gray
                    if return_plot and show_regression:
                        fit_lines.append(
                            p.line(x=t_theor, y=A_theor, line_color="gray")
                        )
                except:
                    print(
                        f"WARNING: {sugar}, {well}, {ODr} has no data in OD range; skipping."
                    )

    # Add the fit lines to the legend
    if return_plot and show_regression:
        legend_items.append(("regression", fit_lines))

    # Make a data frame from the list of results
    df_growth_rates = pl.DataFrame(results)

    if return_plot:
        # Create the legend from the items
        legend = bokeh.models.Legend(items=legend_items, click_policy="hide")
    
        # Add the legend to the plot
        p.add_layout(legend, "right")

        return df_growth_rates, p
    else:
        return p
